title: Maximum Height of a Triangle
summary: Given the counts of red and blue balls, arrange them in a triangular pattern where each row increases by one ball, with same-colored balls in each row and alternating colors between rows.
statement: Given the counts of red and blue balls, arrange them in a triangular pattern where each row increases by one ball, with same-colored balls in each row and alternating colors between rows. Return the highest possible triangle height.
constraints: Build rows of lengths one, two, three, and so on.
Each row uses one color and adjacent rows must alternate colors.
Return the maximum complete height using at most red red balls and blue blue balls; either color may start.
hints: For a fixed starting color, row colors and required counts are forced.
Simulate increasing row lengths until the needed color lacks enough balls.
Repeat with the colors exchanged and take the larger height.
Each simulation greedily builds every possible prefix, and the two starts exhaust all valid triangles.
editorial: Each simulation greedily builds every possible prefix, and the two starts exhaust all valid triangles.

tests.explanation: Starting red uses one red, two blue, and three red cannot fit; starting blue reaches height three.
Rows of one red and two blue cannot fit, but one blue then two red gives height two.
